narrativeProgression.description: Prof. C introduces the Eliza effect, noting that people often attribute human-like characteristics to non-human AIs.
Origin of the name from the 1960s program Eliza.
Functionality of Eliza explained as a simple program that mirrored user input and asked basic questions.
Despite its simplicity, Eliza convinced some users it understood them, showcasing the effect's power.
Underlining mechanism revealed: both Eliza and modern AIs operate on predetermined rules for processing inputs and generating outputs.
Attributing human-like qualities to AI is a human tendency known as anthropomorphism.

youtube_description:
In AI discussion on YouTube you will often find people who attribute human-like characteristics, emotions, and intentions to non-human AIs.
This is often referred to as the ELIZA effect, named after a program from the 1960s ELIZA. This simple program basically parroted a user responses back to them and ask some basic questions. Despite its rudimentary design, ELIZA managed to convince some users that it truly understood their emotions and concerns. 
ELIZA and modern AIs process inputs and generate output based on predetermined rules. Its us humans that attribute human-like characteristics, emotions, and intentions to non-human entities. This is called Anthropomorphism, and it is rooted in our ancient ancestors' mythologies, where they personified natural elements and animals. When someone tells you that an AI thinks, It is likely they are experiencing the Eliza effect.
